mainTopic: Ladders, trees, and ditches between two חצרות: when they count as an opening or a divider for עירוב
overview: רב יוסף asks רבה a series of questions about a ladder that joins two חצרות so they can share one עירוב. If footholds are carved into the wall to widen a narrow ladder, they need to be ten טפחים high. If the whole 'ladder' is carved into the wall, it must reach the top, because bare grooves are hard to climb. רב יוסף then asks about a tree, which may not be climbed on שבת, and an אשירה, which may not be used for any benefit. The גמרא shows that each question could go either way, using the image of a doorway with a lion lying in it. רבה rules that a tree works but an אשירה does not. רב חסדא argues the reverse: only a שבת prohibition should matter for a שבת law. A teaching of רבי אלעזר (some say רבי יוחנן) supports him, while רב נחמן בר יצחק ties both cases to known disputes. A new משנה then teaches that a deep ditch between two חצרות divides them unless it is filled with dirt or pebbles, and that a board four טפחים wide makes a passage across it. The גמרא explains why hay does not fill the ditch. It then begins asking whether dirt fills it without ביטול, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How high must footholds go when they complete a narrow ladder?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks: if a ladder is too narrow and footholds are carved into the wall to complete the width, how high must the carving reach?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he carved into the wall to complete the ladder, how much must he carve?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף asks רבה a practical question. The ladder is narrower than four טפחים, and grooves are carved into the wall beside it to make up the needed width. How high must those grooves go?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that a ladder about four טפחים wide makes the wall count as 'open' between the two חצרות. Here the ladder alone is too narrow, so the carved grooves fill in the missing width. The question is how tall that filled-in section must be for the whole thing to count.

keyTerms.meaning: He carved or dug out (grooves into the wall)
To complete (to make up the missing width of the ladder)
Wall (here, the wall between the two courtyards)
How much? (asking for a measurement)

phrases.english: If he carved into the wall to complete [the ladder's width],
phrases.notes: The real ladder is narrower than four handbreadths. The carved grooves extend its rungs into the wall.

phrases.english: how much [high must it be]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יוסף's series of questions to רבה about ladders in the wall between two חצרות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum height of carved grooves that complete the width of a too-narrow ladder.

steps.title: Ten handbreadths is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the carved section must be ten טפחים high.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Ten handbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers that if the carved-out section reaches ten טפחים, it is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten טפחים is the standard height that gives a wall or space legal significance. Once the combined ladder and grooves are four wide and ten high, the setup counts as a usable passage.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him
Ten (handbreadths)

phrases.english: He said to him: With ten [handbreadths].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The carved section that completes the ladder needs to be ten טפחים high.

steps.title: What if the entire ladder is carved into the wall?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks: if there is no real ladder and all the steps are carved into the wall, how high must they go?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If he carved the whole thing into the wall, how much?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף asks a follow-up question. Now there is no real ladder at all, only steps carved into the wall. How high must they reach?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 1, the grooves only helped a real ladder. Here the grooves are the entire 'ladder'. רב יוסף wants to know whether the same ten-טפחים measure applies.

keyTerms.meaning: He carved it (the ladder)
All of it, entirely

phrases.english: He said to him: If he carved it entirely into the wall,
phrases.notes: There is no wooden ladder. All the steps are grooves in the wall.

phrases.english: how much [high must it be]?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲקָקוֹ כּוּלּוֹ בַּכּוֹתֶל, בְּכַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question that removes the real ladder entirely.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The required height when the whole ladder consists of grooves carved into the wall.

steps.title: The steps must reach the full height of the wall
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the carved steps must go all the way up the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Its full height.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers that here, ten טפחים is not enough. The carved steps must reach the full height of the wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a stricter rule than in step 2. Without a real ladder, the grooves must go all the way to the top before the wall counts as 'open'.

keyTerms.meaning: Its full height (the entire height of the wall)

phrases.english: He said to him: Its full height.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 with a stricter measurement than in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A fully carved ladder must reach the full height of the wall.

steps.title: Why is a fully carved ladder treated differently?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges the difference: why is ten טפחים enough in one case but the full height required in the other?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difference?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges רבה's two answers. In both cases there are carved grooves, so why do they need different heights?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rulings seem inconsistent. Grooves are grooves, so it seems odd that they need only ten טפחים in one case but the whole wall in the other. רב יוסף asks רבה to explain the logic behind the distinction.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difference? (asking why two similar cases get different rulings)

phrases.english: And what is the difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the apparent inconsistency between the answers in steps 2 and 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's different height requirements in steps 2 and 4
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cases involve grooves carved into the wall, so they should seemingly need the same height.

steps.title: A real ladder is easy to climb, but bare grooves are not
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that with a real ladder one can easily climb to the top, but bare grooves are hard to climb.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, one can climb up easily; here, one cannot climb up easily.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains the difference. Where there is a real ladder, a person can easily get up the wall. With only grooves, climbing is hard, so they must reach all the way to the top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is whether people can actually use the setup to pass from one חצר to the other. A real ladder makes climbing easy, so a ten-טפחים base is enough. Bare grooves do not make climbing easy, so they count only if they reach the top.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in the first case, with a real ladder)
Here (in the second case, with only carved grooves)
He can climb up easily

steps.whatToRemember: A ladder joins two חצרות only if it can really be used to cross. A real ladder plus grooves needs ten טפחים. Grooves alone must reach the top of the wall, because they are hard to climb.
steps.confusionAlert: 'מסתלק ליה' does not mean 'it is removed'. Here it means 'he can go up easily'.

phrases.english: He said to him: There, one can climb up easily;
phrases.notes: With a real ladder, it is easy to reach the top.

phrases.english: here, one cannot climb up easily.
phrases.notes: With only grooves, climbing is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם מִסְתַּלֵּק לֵיהּ, הָכָא לָא מִסְתַּלֵּק לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Carved grooves should need the same height in both cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ease of climbing decides the measurement. A real ladder is easy to climb, so ten טפחים is enough. Bare grooves are hard to climb, so they must reach the full height.

steps.title: Can a tree serve as the ladder?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks רבה what the law is if someone designates a tree as the ladder between the two חצרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף asked רבה: If he made the tree into a ladder, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף asks a new question. A tree stands next to the wall and is easy to climb. Does it count as a ladder that makes the wall 'open'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tree is physically easy to climb. However, the רבנן forbade climbing trees on שבת. So the question is whether something that may not be used on שבת can still count as a passage.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him (a formal question or dilemma)
He made it into, designated it as
Tree
Ladder
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef asked of Rabba:
If he made the tree into a ladder,
what is the law?
phrases.notes: Climbing a tree on שבת is rabbinically forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף מֵרַבָּה: עֲשָׂאוֹ לָאִילָן סוּלָּם, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about a tree, building on the idea that ease of climbing matters.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a tree, which may not be climbed on שבת, can count as a ladder that connects two חצרות.

steps.title: The question applies according to both רבי and רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the tree question can be asked according to רבי and also according to רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it be asked according to רבי, and let it be asked according to the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that this question can be asked according to both sides of a known disagreement. It is setting up the next move, which will explain why each side has room for doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי and רבנן disagree about an עירוב תחומין placed in a tree. רבי holds it is valid, and רבנן disagree. You might think each one's view already settles the tree question. The גמרא says no: neither opinion settles it on its own. Steps 9–10 explain why, and רבה answers in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be asked (the question applies)
רבי יהודה הנשיא
The Sages (the majority opinion)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the tree question is not just a repeat of the רבי–רבנן disagreement about an עירוב in a tree. It is a separate issue that each opinion still needs to answer.

phrases.english: Let it be asked according to Rabbi,
phrases.notes: רבי holds that an עירוב placed in a tree is valid.

phrases.english: let it be asked according to the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The רבנן disagree with רבי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the scope of the question in step 7 and sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Showing that the tree question is not settled by either side of the רבי–רבנן dispute.

steps.title: Why the tree question is unclear even according to רבי
steps.stepSummary: רבי allowed an עירוב in a tree because a שבות does not apply at בין השמשות. That leniency may not cover a ladder that must work all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ask it according to רבי. רבי only said there that the rabbis did not decree on anything forbidden because of שבות. That applies only at בין השמשות, but not for the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the tree question is real according to רבי. His known leniency might not reach this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere, רבי holds that an עירוב placed in a tree works, because the rabbis did not apply their decrees at בין השמשות, the doubtful twilight moment. But an opening between two חצרות has to be usable all of שבת. During the day, climbing a tree is fully forbidden, so even רבי might say the tree is not a valid ladder.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the question be asked (according to a given opinion)
He only said this far (his ruling is limited to that case)
A rabbinic prohibition on שבת, such as climbing a tree
Twilight, the doubtful time between day and night
The whole day

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as רבי ruling that the tree fails. The גמרא is only showing why someone could think so, which is what makes it a real question.

phrases.english: Let it be asked according to Rabbi:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi only said there
phrases.notes: Refers to the case of an עירוב placed in a tree.

phrases.english: that anything forbidden because of a rabbinic Shabbat prohibition
they did not decree against it
that applies only at twilight,
but for the whole day, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבִּי: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first side of the two-sided question raised in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי's leniency about שבות at בין השמשות also make a tree count as a ladder that must work all day?

steps.title: Why the tree might work even according to רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Even רבנן might call the tree a real opening. The ban on climbing it is just an outside obstacle, like a lion lying in a doorway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps even according to רבנן: it is an opening, and it is just that a lion is crouching on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the question. Even the stricter רבנן might accept the tree as a valid opening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן rejected an עירוב in a tree because the food had to be truly reachable at בין השמשות. Here nobody actually has to climb. The tree only needs to have the status of an opening. A doorway with a lion lying in it is still a doorway even though no one can pass, so the ban on climbing may not cancel the tree's status.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
An opening or doorway
A lion
That crouches or lies down

steps.whyThisMatters: The lion image is a well-known principle. A physical or legal obstacle that blocks practical use does not erase something's basic status as an opening.

phrases.english: Or perhaps even according to the Rabbis:
it is an opening,
and it is just a lion crouching on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the question from step 9, so the question has two real possibilities.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Might even רבנן treat the tree as a valid opening, since the ban on climbing is only an outside obstacle?
steps.whatToRemember: The tree question has two real sides. According to רבי, the tree might fail because it must work all day. According to רבנן, it might succeed because it is like a doorway with a lion in it. רבה answers the question in step 15.

steps.title: New question: an אשירה used as a ladder
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks what the law is if someone sets up an אשירה, an idolatrous tree that one may not benefit from, as the ladder.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he made an אשירה into a ladder, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new but similar question is asked. This time the tree is an אשירה, which is forbidden for any benefit at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with a regular tree was only the שבת ban on climbing. An אשירה adds a stronger problem: all benefit from it is forbidden, every day of the week. The question is whether such a tree can still count as a ladder joining the two חצרות.

keyTerms.meaning: He made it into
A tree worshipped as idolatry, forbidden for any benefit
A ladder
What is the law?

phrases.english: If he made an asheira into a ladder, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a regular tree to an idolatrous tree, building on רב יוסף's question in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does an אשירה, which is forbidden for all benefit, count as a valid ladder between two חצרות?

steps.title: The אשירה question applies according to both opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the אשירה question can be asked according to רבי יהודה and also according to רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it be asked according to רבי יהודה, and let it be asked according to רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא announces that the question is open under both opinions and is about to explain each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה and רבנן disagree elsewhere about placing an עירוב in a place one may not benefit from. The גמרא signals that neither opinion clearly decides the אשירה case. This sets up the explanations that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who is lenient about using a forbidden place for an עירוב
The Sages who disagree with him

phrases.english: Let it be asked according to Rabbi Yehuda; let it be asked according to the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Frames the step 11 question as open under both opinions, the same way step 8 framed the tree question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How would each side of the רבי יהודה and רבנן dispute rule on an אשירה used as a ladder?

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה's leniency might not cover an אשירה ladder
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה allows making an עירוב in a place one may not benefit from. But there the person does not care what happens to the place after the עירוב takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ask it according to רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה only said there that one may acquire a home in a place forbidden for benefit because, after the עירוב has acquired the home for him, he does not care whether it is guarded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why even the lenient רבי יהודה might not allow an אשירה as a ladder. The other half of the contrast, a ladder that he wants to keep using, is understood rather than spelled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה lets someone set an עירוב in a forbidden place, such as near a grave. He needs it only for the moment the עירוב takes effect and gets no lasting benefit afterward. A ladder is different, because he wants it to stay in place and serve him all שבת. That ongoing use could count as forbidden benefit from the אשירה.

keyTerms.meaning: To acquire a home (to establish one's שבת residence through the עירוב)
Things one is forbidden to benefit from
The food placed to set one's שבת residence
He does not care, or it does not matter to him
That it be guarded or preserved

phrases.english: Let it be asked according to Rabbi Yehuda:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda only said there
that it is permitted to acquire a home with things forbidden for benefit,
only there,
because after the eruv has acquired the home for him
he does not care whether it is guarded.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the רבי יהודה side of the question announced in step 12, following the same pattern as step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יהודה's leniency, which relies on the person not caring about the place afterward, extend to a ladder he wants to keep using?

steps.title: Maybe even רבנן would call the אשירה an opening
steps.stepSummary: The second side of רב יוסף's question: maybe even רבנן agree that an אשירה counts as an opening, with its איסור being only an outside obstacle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps even according to the רבנן, it is an opening, and there is just a lion crouching on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question about the אשירה by giving the other possibility, according to רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן do not allow an עירוב in a forbidden place. Still, maybe they would say an אשירה ladder is different. The tree really is a usable path, and the איסור הנאה only blocks it from the outside, like a lion lying in a doorway. A doorway with a lion in it is still a doorway.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. This opens the second side of a question.
An opening or doorway
A lion crouching on it. This is an outside obstacle that does not cancel the opening.

steps.confusionAlert: Step 10 used the same lion image for a regular tree and the rule against climbing it. Here the lion image is applied to the אשירה and its איסור הנאה.

phrases.english: Or perhaps, even according to the Rabbis:
it is an opening,
phrases.notes: The אשירה physically works as a ladder.

phrases.english: and a lion is crouching upon it.
phrases.notes: The איסור is just an outside blocker.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 13 gave the רבי יהודה side of the question. This step gives the רבנן side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the איסור הנאה on an אשירה cancel its status as an opening, or is it only an outside obstacle?

steps.title: A regular tree works but an idolatrous tree does not
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that a regular tree is permitted as a ladder, but an אשירה is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A tree is permitted, but an אשירה is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers both of רב יוסף's questions at once: a regular tree counts as a ladder, but an אשירה does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה treats the two cases differently. The rule against climbing a regular tree is only a light rabbinic שבות, so the tree still counts as an opening. The איסור הנאה on an אשירה is more serious, so it does cancel the opening.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree
Permitted / forbidden

phrases.english: He said to him: A tree is permitted,
but an asheira is prohibited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both of רב יוסף's questions: the tree question (steps 7–10) and the אשירה question (steps 11–14).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A regular tree counts as a ladder and opening. An אשירה does not.

steps.title: רב חסדא argues the reverse: the tree should be forbidden and the idolatrous tree permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא objects. A tree is blocked by a שבת rule, so it should not count for שבת. An אשירה is blocked by an unrelated rule, so it should count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא objected: On the contrary! A tree, which is blocked by a שבת prohibition, should be forbidden. An אשירה, which is blocked by a different prohibition, should not be forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא challenges רבה's answer and argues the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We are deciding whether a ladder works for a שבת law. If the thing blocking the ladder is itself a שבת rule, like the שבות against climbing a tree, it would be strange to ignore it in a שבת matter. The איסור on an אשירה has nothing to do with שבת, so for שבת purposes it is just a lion in the doorway, and the opening still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to it
On the contrary. The opposite is more logical.
A prohibition that comes from the laws of שבת
A prohibition from some other area of law, unrelated to שבת

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not saying an אשירה may be used. Benefiting from it is still forbidden. He only means that its איסור does not cancel its status as an opening for the laws of שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda strongly objects to this:
On the contrary, a tree,
where a Shabbat prohibition causes it, should be prohibited.

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֵׁירָה שֶׁאִיסּוּר דָּבָר אַחֵר גּוֹרֵם לוֹ
phrases.english: An asheira, where a prohibition of something else causes it,
should not be prohibited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבה's answer in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that a tree is permitted and an אשירה is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For a שבת matter, only a שבת prohibition should cancel the opening. So the tree should be forbidden and the אשירה permitted, the exact reverse of רבה's ruling.

steps.title: A teaching from ארץ ישראל (רבי אלעזר or רבי יוחנן) supports רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports, in the name of רבי אלעזר (some say רבי אבהו in the name of רבי יוחנן), the same principle as רב חסדא. A blocker caused by a שבת rule forbids, and a blocker caused by another rule does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי אלעזר (and some say רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן): Anything blocked by a שבת prohibition is forbidden. Anything blocked by some other prohibition is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching from ארץ ישראל that states רב חסדא's exact principle, supporting his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase איתמר נמי signals backup from another source. This teaching (from רבי אלעזר, or in the other version רבי יוחנן) turns רב חסדא's logic into a general rule. In questions of שבת, only a שבת-based איסור cancels something's function, while איסורים from other areas are ignored. So the tree does not count, and the אשירה does.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated. This introduces support from another source.
When רבין came from ארץ ישראל to בבל
And some say. This gives an alternate chain of transmission.

steps.whatToRemember: The principle: for שבת purposes, a blocker that comes from a שבת rule (like the tree) cancels the opening. A blocker that comes from an unrelated איסור (like the אשירה) does not. This is רב חסדא's view, backed by רבי אלעזר (or, in another version, רבי יוחנן). Step 18 gives רב נחמן בר יצחק's different version.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule for שבת and עירוב laws. Only איסורים that belong to שבת itself are taken into account when deciding whether something counts as an opening or a valid access.

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said that Rabbi Elazar said,
and some say Rabbi Abbahu said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאִיסּוּר שַׁבָּת גָּרַם לוֹ — אָסוּר,
phrases.english: Anything where a Shabbat prohibition caused it is prohibited;

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאִיסּוּר דָּבָר אַחֵר גָּרַם לוֹ — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: anything where a prohibition of something else caused it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's objection in step 16 with an independent tradition.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's principle that only a שבת-based איסור cancels the opening.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבין's report in the name of רבי אלעזר, or רבי אבהו in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Something blocked by a שבת prohibition does not count. Something blocked by an unrelated prohibition does count.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק ties both cases to known disputes
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק teaches a different version. The tree case depends on the argument between רבי and רבנן. The אשירה case depends on the argument between רבי יהודה and רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק taught it this way: the tree depends on the dispute between רבי and the רבנן. The אשירה depends on the dispute between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of the earlier discussion. In this version, each case depends on an argument we already know about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף had tried to treat these as open questions, separate from the known disputes. רב נחמן בר יצחק says each one depends on an existing argument. For the tree, רבי permits it and the רבנן forbid it. For the אשירה, the question is whether a forbidden object can serve for an עירוב: רבי יהודה says yes and the רבנן say no.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught it this way (a different version of the discussion)
A dispute between authorities
A tree
A tree that is worshipped as an idol. No one may benefit from it.

steps.whatToRemember: In רב נחמן בר יצחק's version, there is no new question here. The tree depends on the argument between רבי and רבנן. The אשירה depends on the argument between רבי יהודה and רבנן.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַתְנֵי הָכִי:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak taught it this way:
A tree: this is the dispute of Rebbi and the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: רבי permits using the tree as a ladder. The רבנן forbid it.

phrases.english: An asheira: this is the dispute of Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: This is the argument about making an עירוב in a place one may not benefit from.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַתְנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the whole discussion, linking each case to a known dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The tree depends on the dispute between רבי and רבנן. The אשירה depends on the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבנן.

steps.title: A ditch between two courtyards, and what fills it
steps.stepSummary: A ditch ten טפחים deep and four wide between two courtyards splits them, so each must make its own עירוב. Straw or hay in the ditch does not change this. Dirt or pebbles do: the ditch is erased, and the courtyards make one עירוב together.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ditch between two courtyards that is ten deep and four wide: they make two עירובין, not one. This is true even if it is full of straw or hay. If it is full of dirt or pebbles, they make one עירוב, not two.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a deep, wide ditch acts like a wall between two courtyards, and explains what kind of filling erases it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ditch of this size counts as a full divider, so the two courtyards cannot join in one עירוב. Straw and hay are not seen as a lasting fill, so the ditch still stands. Dirt and pebbles stay put, so the ditch counts as gone and the two courtyards become one area.

keyTerms.meaning: A ditch or trench
Courtyards
They make two separate עירובין, one for each courtyard
Straw or hay
Dirt or pebbles

steps.confusionAlert: Two עירובין means the courtyards are separate. One עירוב means they count as one shared area. With dirt or pebbles, they are not allowed to make two.

phrases.english: Mishnah: A ditch that is between two courtyards,
ten handbreadths deep and four wide:
they make two eruvin, and they do not make one.
This is true even if it is full of straw or hay.
phrases.notes: Straw or hay is not seen as a lasting fill.

phrases.english: If it is full of dirt or pebbles:
they make one eruv, and they do not make two.
phrases.notes: The ditch counts as erased.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ditch ten deep and four wide divides two courtyards, even when it holds straw or hay. Dirt or pebbles erase it, so the courtyards make one עירוב.

steps.title: A board across the ditch, and balconies facing each other
steps.stepSummary: A board four טפחים wide across the ditch, or between two facing balconies, makes a passage. The residents may then make two עירובין or one, as they choose. A board narrower than four טפחים does not count, so they must make two.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he put a board four טפחים wide across it, and likewise with two balconies facing each other: they make two עירובין, and if they want, they make one. If it is less than this, they make two, not one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It teaches that a wide enough board works like a doorway between the two areas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A board four טפחים wide counts as an opening. The two areas are still separate, but connected, so the residents may choose to join or stay apart. A narrower board is not a real passage, so the areas stay fully divided.

keyTerms.meaning: A board or plank
Balconies that stick out from buildings
And if they want (it is their choice)
Less than this size

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same idea as the earlier ladder and tree cases. A real way to cross between two areas counts as an opening, and that opening lets them join in one עירוב.

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן עָלָיו נֶסֶר שֶׁרָחָב אַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים,
phrases.english: If he placed on it a board that is four handbreadths wide,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן שְׁתֵּי גְזוּזְטְרָאוֹת זוֹ כְּנֶגֶד זוֹ —
phrases.english: and likewise two balconies facing one another:

phrases.aramaic: מְעָרְבִין שְׁנַיִם, וְאִם רָצוּ מְעָרְבִין אֶחָד.
phrases.english: they make two eruvin, and if they want, they make one.
If it is less than this:
they make two eruvin, and they do not make one.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָתַן עָלָיו נֶסֶר שֶׁרָחָב אַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by adding a board as a way to cross the ditch.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A board four טפחים wide makes an opening, so the residents may choose one עירוב or two. A narrower board does not, so they must make two.

steps.title: Challenge: another משנה treats hay as a real wall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why hay does not fill the ditch. Another משנה teaches that a haystack ten טפחים high between two courtyards counts as a wall, so they must make two עירובין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does hay not count as a filling? But we learned: a haystack between two courtyards that is ten טפחים high — they make two עירובין, and they do not make one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion with a challenge. It questions the משנה's rule that hay does not fill the ditch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה treats hay in a ditch as if it is not there. But the other משנה treats a haystack as solid enough to be a wall. If hay counts as a lasting divider there, it should count as a lasting fill here and erase the ditch. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: fills in the ditch so that it counts as gone
But didn't we learn (introduces a source that seems to contradict)
A haystack

phrases.english: Gemara: And does hay not fill in the ditch?
But didn't we learn in a Mishnah:
A haystack that is between two courtyards,
ten handbreadths high:
they make two eruvin, and they do not make one!
phrases.notes: So hay counts as a real wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתֶבֶן לָא חָיֵיץ? וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the hay ruling in step 19 using a different משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that straw or hay in the ditch does not erase it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The haystack משנה treats hay as a lasting wall. So hay in a ditch should also count as a lasting fill and erase the ditch.

steps.title: Hay always counts as a wall, but fills a ditch only when left there for good
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers the question from step 21. Everyone agrees that hay counts as a מחיצה. For filling a ditch (חציצה), hay works only if the owner nullified it (ביטול) and decided to leave it there permanently.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: About a wall, everyone agrees that hay counts as a wall. But about filling the ditch: if he nullified it (decided to leave it there), it fills the ditch. If he did not nullify it, it does not fill the ditch.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction from step 21. He explains that hay can count as a wall and still not count as filling a ditch, because these are two different questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a wall only needs something physically standing there, so hay counts even if it might be moved later. Erasing a ditch means treating the space as solid ground, which needs the hay to be there for good. So the משנה about the ditch is speaking of hay the owner plans to remove, and that kind of hay does not fill it.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי, an אמורא who gives the answer here
A wall or partition that divides two areas
Everyone agrees; there is no argument
Here: filling or sealing the ditch so it no longer counts as a gap
He nullified it, meaning he decided to leave it there permanently
It fills or seals the ditch

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מחיצה and חציצה here. מחיצה means a wall that separates. חציצה in this line means filling the ditch, which actually joins the two courtyards together. Hay can count as a wall without counting as filling.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea for the rest of the סוגיא. Whether something fills a space can depend on the owner's intent (ביטול), not only on what is physically there.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
With regard to a partition —
everyone agrees
phrases.notes: Literally: 'the whole world does not argue'

phrases.english: that it is a partition,
phrases.notes: Hay ten טפחים high divides the courtyards.

phrases.english: but with regard to filling the ditch,
if he nullified it — it fills,
phrases.notes: He decided to leave the hay there permanently.

phrases.english: and if he did not nullify it — it does not fill.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לְעִנְיַן מְחִיצָה כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 21 between hay as a wall and hay that does not fill a ditch.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two legal questions (wall vs. filling) and adding the condition of ביטול
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hay should either count everywhere or nowhere, so if it counts as a wall it should also fill the ditch.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hay always counts as a wall. It fills a ditch only if the owner nullified it. The ditch משנה speaks of hay that was not nullified.

steps.title: Does dirt fill the ditch even with no stated intent?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'filled with dirt' and asks whether this works even without ביטול. It brings a משנה about טומאת מת: a house filled with hay or pebbles is nullified only if the owner nullified the filling. This passage ends as the גמרא begins drawing the inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'filled with dirt.' Does this apply even with no stated intent? But we learned in a משנה: A house that one filled with hay or pebbles and nullified them — the house is nullified. We can infer: if he nullified it, yes...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that dirt or pebbles automatically fill the ditch. It is setting up an inference from another משנה, which continues past the end of this passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה about the ditch seems to say that dirt fills it on its own, with no mention of intent. But a משנה about a house containing a dead body says pebbles count as filling the house only when the owner nullified them. The words 'if he nullified it — yes' begin to show that ביטול is needed, so even pebbles should not work automatically.

keyTerms.meaning: Filled with dirt; the quoted words from the משנה
With no stated intent; left without any decision
But we learned in a משנה; introduces a source used to challenge
Pebbles
It is nullified; here, the house no longer counts as a house
Yes

steps.confusionAlert: The house משנה is about טומאת מת, not עירובין. The גמרא borrows it only to learn when a filling counts as permanent.

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] filled with dirt.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה's ruling that dirt or pebbles erase the ditch.

phrases.english: And even with no stated intent?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
A house that one filled with hay or pebbles
and nullified it — it is nullified.
phrases.notes: The house now counts as a sealed grave for טומאת מת and is no longer a house.

phrases.english: If he nullified it — yes,
phrases.notes: Start of the inference; the next passage continues: if not, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי made ביטול the condition for hay, the גמרא asks whether the משנה's dirt and pebbles also need ביטול.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in step 19 that dirt or pebbles in the ditch erase it and allow one עירוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about a house shows that hay or pebbles count as filling only with ביטול. So dirt or pebbles in the ditch should also need ביטול, yet the ditch משנה gives no such condition.
